minimal_definition_only_context: A measure assigns extended nonnegative masses to measurable sets; IsProbabilityMeasure means mass of the whole space is one. A kernel assigns each input a measure measurably. Countable and MeasurableSingletonClass mean countability and measurability of all singleton sets.
Fin(n+1) is a finite index type with n+1 elements; Bool is a two-element measurable type. The state is the full function space on those coordinates.

The kernel in the second proposition is an equal-weight state-independent mixture, with weight1/(n+1) per coordinate. For i, split x into (retained tuple,x_i) by a measurable equivalence e_i and map the target through e_i; at retained value a take the product of the Dirac measure at a and the selected regular conditional distribution of the second coordinate given the first, then map through e_i inverse.

The regular conditional distribution here is Mathlib's chosen Markov conditional law, specified only almost everywhere under the retained marginal. The definition stipulates no pointwise normalized-fiber formula at null retained values.
Kernel.IsReversible means that for every pair of measurable sets A,B the lower integral of κ(x,B) over A under μ equals the lower integral of κ(y,A) over B under μ.
